# The learned policy (WSP)

## When it applies
robo.policy lets a policy learned from demonstrations drive both arms, a few chunks of 24 steps at a time. It acts on the images and one sentence. From what it was shown it may know how a thing is physically done, and it moves in one smooth go, without stopping to measure. But it does not reason: it cannot decide from what is in view which thing goes where or what comes next, and rewording the sentence hardly steers it. It takes the wrong arm or the wrong thing, misses small targets and tight fits, sweeps through what stands in its way, and knows nothing of what must not be touched or how many steps are left; what it does wrong may not be repairable. It was shown work from an ordinary beginning: it does best while the things it has to handle still stand as they started, and it has rarely recovered what has fallen over, slipped into an odd pose or been left half placed.

Do the work yourself whenever you can state each step and what it must look like. A single miss or a refused plan is ordinary: measure again and change the approach. When the same thing has failed twice, the limits above do not rule it out, and what the policy would have to handle still stands as it started, give it a try; what has fallen or lies oddly, set right yourself or leave.

The policy is an optional way to act, not the default. What it did before only suggests a general capability; it is no routing by name, no promise of success and no table of task scores, and similar geometry can still fail with another layout, contact, constraint or weight version. Flash (profile="flash") suits a continuous local action where the current view is enough, the target is single and clear, and the tolerance is generous. Memory (profile="memory") suits a local action whose needed history is really covered by its own continuous view; on its first call, or after a switch, it starts from the current frame and cannot recover what you saw and it did not. Fine insertion or fitting, a required contact pose, comparing arbitrary properties or following identity and order rules, matching a moving target, complex discrete interactions and extra subgoals kept only in your memory have been unstable with it: by default do them with the native tools. This is no permanent ban on a kind of action: hand such a step over again only when the instruction itself and the policy's own observation fully express the local goal and real feedback supports it.

## How
Give it the instruction word for word, about four chunks at a time. Before each new hand-over, say what you see that makes it suitable, what change you expect next, and whether the step needs fine control, your own memory, or history that really reached the memory profile. Your descriptions, object references, Skill plans and notes are not passed to it.

## Checks
Look at the images after each call: go on while the job visibly advances as it should, and take over when two calls show nothing or it disturbs what was right; repeating does not make it better. Whether the policy finished a local motion and whether the job is done are checked separately: a call that returned is not a motion that succeeded, and "still moving" is no substitute for checking progress.

## Recovery
Afterwards nothing you measured holds: read robo.state for what the hands hold, and measure again. A wrong direction, a risk or doubt means take over at once with the native tools. After calls in a row without progress, let both profiles rest: only a real native correction and a fresh observation justify another hand-over, and switching between flash and memory to gamble on success is not one. Finish with the native tools: release, withdraw and return with robo.home, and check the state.
